item.text: {"summary":"Fix decimal rounding in the fast floating-point formatter.","explanation":"The fast path rounds a value with `{:#.0f}` using `fmt::format(\"{:#.0f}\", 0.5)`: the assertion expects `\"0.\"`, but the formatter returns `\"1.\"`. Its zero-precision check rounds an exact halfway value up, even though ties should round to the even digit. In `format_test.precision_rounding`, `fmt::format(\"{:.3f}\", 0.0015)` is expected to produce `\"0.002\"` but produces `\"0.003\"`; `fmt::format(\"{:.3}\", 0.00123)` is expected to produce `\"0.00123\"` but produces `\"0.00124\"`. The fast path increments the final decimal digit by two, causing both excess-rounding results. Restrict zero-precision rounding to values strictly above halfway, or values exactly halfway with additional nonzero digits, and increment retained digits by one.","edits":[{"path":"include/fmt/format.h","old":"          if ((first_segment | static_cast<uint64_t>(has_more_segments)) >=\n              5000000000000000000ULL) {","new":"          if (first_segment > 5000000000000000000ULL ||\n              (first_segment == 5000000000000000000ULL && has_more_segments)) {"},{"path":"include/fmt/format.h","old":"          buf[precision - 1] += 2;","new":"          buf[precision - 1] += 1;"}]}
